scope: Representative shared REST HTTP/JSON comparisons plus explicitly pending domain/DB/WebSocket obligations; not exhaustive coverage of all 359 Java inventory rows.
inventory_policy: Java inventory rows are source anchors, not proof of Rust implementation or parity. Executable cases use methods/paths registered in current Rust build_router and Java controllers. Rust feature flags default off. Pending endpoints are obligations, not claims of route/behavior equivalence.

execution.base_urls: Separate origin URLs without a trailing /api; fixture paths already include /api. Use isolated Java and Rust processes, never production.
prerequisites: bash, curl, jq and diff available; both services already started and reachable.
Enable every required_rust_flags value listed in domains; record effective flags and backend source revisions in execution evidence.
Java requires its complete isolated schema for startup. The committed anonymous requests do not query DB after missing-token/device rejection and do not mutate business data.
Use UTC for the Java JVM and keep the month-window case inside one UTC calendar month. If this precondition cannot hold, record it blocked rather than ignore differences.
Literal phase9-not-a-credential/device strings are invalid sentinels, not credentials. No real token/device/password may be committed in this fixture, manifest or result.
execution.request_schema: Top-level array. Runner consumes only method/path/headers/body; case_id and domain are metadata. method/path are literal, headers are literal, body is JSON serialized by jq.
supported: Sequential same-method/path/headers/body requests to Java then Rust
JSON comparison after jq -S object-key ordering; array ordering and number/string/null/absent distinctions remain visible
unsupported: Expected status or business-code assertions (oracles below are documentation, not executable runner fields)
Per-backend requests/credentials, environment interpolation, login response capture or dynamic ID substitution
Multipart, raw non-JSON body, binary downloads, response-header assertions
Database seeding/reset/snapshot/assertions, clock injection, random-source control
WebSocket upgrades/messages/recipient sets, asynchronous barriers, lifecycle orchestration
Field masking, timestamp tolerances, semantic numeric coercion, array sorting
Structured result writing; this result JSON is not updated by the runner
execution.acceptance_caveat: Exit 0 only reports equality, not correctness: equal 404/500/business errors are not successful domain reads. Runner process-substitution jq failures may leave two empty diff streams; valid JSON and expected HTTP/business oracles must be checked by the evidence collector before claiming acceptance. No acceptance is claimed here.
evidence_required: Record fixture revision, case_id/index, both backend source revisions, effective flags, isolated schema seed/reset identity and clock/timezone configuration.

Capture both HTTP statuses and redacted JSON responses, start/end timestamps, exit code and comparison result for every executed case. Credentials must never appear in saved requests, command logs, URLs or response artifacts.
Record outcomes individually as EXECUTED_MATCH, EXECUTED_DIFFERENCE, EXECUTION_ERROR or BLOCKED_PRECONDITION. A pending/not-run case is never PASS.
Archive observed artifacts before updating result metadata; one earlier semantic probe must not be relabeled as execution of this fixture.

determinism.current_normalization: Only jq -S object-key ordering, exactly as the existing runner. No fields are dropped, arrays reordered or scalar types coerced.
determinism.credentials: For future authenticated cases generate one-use synthetic credentials in memory, store only matching token digests/device bindings in the two isolated schemas, and materialize runtime headers via a non-persistent input. Runner requires a file path and has no header injection. An external collector must redact error output because login/profile bodies may contain secrets.
determinism.databases: Never point both writers at the same schema. Start each scenario from independently cloned identical schema/data, disable unrelated background work or drive it at a named barrier, and restore both before the next scenario. Fixed primary keys/FKs and explicit timestamps are preferred.
determinism.identifiers: If a write generates UUID/autoincrement/session IDs, use a separate harness to correlate IDs by synthetic business key and rewrite dependent requests per backend. Do not delete all id fields to make a diff pass; preserve references and prove relationships.
determinism.clock: Prefer fixed input timestamps and controlled clock. If either backend cannot accept the same clock, timing-sensitive responses are not eligible for exact fixture comparison; the separate harness must specify intervals/tolerances and verify durations, ordering and state transitions, never mask scoring/time fields wholesale.
determinism.ordering: One-row seeds avoid unspecified SQL ordering for basic reads. Multi-row ordering and pagination require unique sort keys and exact expected arrays; never globally sort response arrays to hide ordering defects.
determinism.randomness: Use an explicit stored question/cable/term selection or a one-candidate pool; do not compare independently randomized samples as exact JSON.
determinism.db_assertions: Separate harness snapshots named target and non-target rows from the entity tables in schema-inventory.tsv before/after each step. Compare inserted/deleted key sets, owner/FK relationships, numeric score/time/state/attempt values and atomic rollback; rejected owner/admin/terminal operations must leave both target and unrelated rows unchanged. HTTP equality alone proves none of these.
determinism.websocket: Compare ordered frames per connection, recipients, opcode, payload JSON types and close behavior using stable session/room/user aliases. Correlate only generated identifiers; do not reorder messages or ignore extra broadcasts. Query credentials are runtime-only and must be scrubbed from traces.

excluded_from_shared_rest_fixture.reason: Rust infrastructure health shapes do not have matching Java controller contracts in the active REST inventory; use backend-specific liveness/readiness smoke, not exact shared JSON equality.
Rust-only diagnostic routes, not active Java business routes. Header-source cases now target shared POST /api/user/getUsersByToken.
No shared JSON controller contract; frontend/static fallback or routing error is not business parity.
Backend-specific OpenAPI documents differ in metadata and surface, and Java can negotiate YAML. A separate semantic API inventory check is required, not whole-document equality.
WebSocket handshake/frame protocol, not ordinary HTTP JSON; use ws.status case.
Two sequential real clock reads cannot be deterministic exact equality; use tools.clock separate harness.

oracle_not_enforced_by_runner.payload: 12 {year,month} objects, descending inclusive from current UTC month; key order irrelevant, array order significant.

domains.setup: No rows needed. Java JVM timezone UTC; Rust uses UTC. Both requests must remain in the same UTC calendar month.

Clone synthetic users A (owner), B (other user), C (administrator with is_admin=0), D (ordinary role is_admin=1), E (no user-role row). Seed the same generated token digest/device pair in each isolated database; keep raw credentials in memory only.
Seed one cable type and one cable with two ordered floor rows; distinct fixed IDs and floor numbers.
Seed two rule types, exactly one default per type, explicit decimal thresholds and stable IDs.
Seed one device type/device/rule, one equipment device/keypoint and one equipment training each for A and B with fixed timestamps.
Seed one classify/knowledge/SWF/test graph, one single-choice and one multiple-choice question, progress for A and B, and fixed file bytes.
Seed one question level, deterministic questions with fixed IDs/answers and one paper with explicit question order/points; no random selection.
Seed paper/answers and two participants with fixed exam IDs. Separate ready/running/submitted records, stable deadlines and an explicitly controlled clock.
Seed fixed owner/other-user IDs and distinct completed, running and empty-category rows; include a non-zero duration/count producing fractional average speed.
Seed owner word-stock and training with a fixed character sequence, one other-user training and a stable clock.
Seed one receive-keypoint and one keypoint for type=1 with stable content, plus another type to detect overbroad updates.
Seed a fixed military term tree and radiotelephone term set; one candidate per random selection query; stable owner/training IDs, owner and other-user records, controlled clock.
Seed fixed telegram/report/log/rule rows with known message groups, A and B ownership and controlled time.
Seed owner and other-user type=1 base rows with fixed timing/value arrays and known grading rule.
Seed base/whole-train records and known text/answer arrays for A and B with stable elapsed-time inputs.
Seed same cable, stage/settings, capture key/time/value arrays and owner training states; use explicit controlled millisecond durations.
Seed ordered message floors and reports, one current and one terminal owner training, one B training, and controlled clock.
Seed same page content and rule, fixed owner/non-owner IDs and attempt/state, ready/running/finished records; preserve capitalized route prefix.
Seed fixed trainType and page IDs, explicit pageSize/pageNumber fields from the Java Page DTO, one final partial page and known receipt text; controlled clock.
Seed settings, masthead and train/page content with explicit IDs, owner A/other B, known capture arrays and controlled time.
Seed known group-net rules/questions/answers and owner/other-user training, fixed IDs and point weights.

Separate fixed key/telex/ticker training graphs, controller role=1 and participant role=0, two participants and one outsider. Explicit attempt, page numbers, known partial last page and controlled clock. Disable spontaneous recovery or drive it at an agreed instant.

Separate router/report/recept/disturb rooms with fixed room/page/channel IDs, creator, member and outsider. Seed identical memberships and no live sockets; then drive both stacks through the same WS barriers.
Seed fixed per-user theory/exam/training records in an explicit year, including zero and non-zero categories; stable time window and user/role IDs.
Seed one global rule per selected type with explicit numeric penalty/threshold values and a separate untouched type.

pending_cases.assertions_required: Record request send/receive time on one synchronized clock; response is numeric epoch milliseconds inside the request interval. Exact sequential equality is not a valid assertion.
Same fixed user/profile/role projections for A; no credential or password fields leak.
Generated unregistered token/device pair returns HTTP200/code206 on both, not a dependency error.
D and E each return HTTP200/code207; C returns only the seeded directory. Authorization is not covered by anonymous code203 cases.

Fresh login uses generated credentials; capture separate response tokens without persisting them. Compare profile projection, token digest changes, logout NULL token/device fields and subsequent code206. Login tokens cannot be byte-compared.
Compare seeded type, nested cable/floor values, nullability and order using the same ID/body on both.
Ordinary user denied; administrator update changes only the target cable/floors; unrelated cable unchanged and delete removes the intended child rows.
Compare numeric JSON thresholds, active/default flags and stable ordering for requested type.
Admin changes one type only; ordinary/no-role denied with no changed rows; default transition must not leave two defaults.
Compare joined fields, JSON numeric/string/null types and token-scoped training lists.
A cannot read B training; forged user identity cannot create B training; device administrator write succeeds and D/E are denied. Compare target and non-target DB rows.
Compare the one seeded graph and question types; use body.id for SWF ID, not swfId.
Submit A progress with a forged B identity; only A progress/score rows change, score comes from stored answers.
Separate multipart harness: text, binary and over-limit files; compare business envelope and stored bytes/path relationship, not generated filenames.
Compare non-empty level/paper graph and question order; not just empty lists.
D/E denied, C writes exact question membership and weights; unchanged unrelated paper. Generated IDs require correlation before comparing dependent requests.
Separate binary harness validates content type/disposition, workbook cells and row order; do not feed binary output to jq.
Compare A own self-test and exam; B cannot read A private result.
Match ready/running/submitted transitions, server-authoritative score and repeated terminal rejection; compare exam, participant and answer rows.
JSON object/array shapes remain JSON; ordinary/no-role denied; administrator changes only selected scores, no cross-exam update.
Compare all categories, numeric avgSpeed including fractional/non-zero values and no cross-user contribution. The archived zero-only probe is insufficient.
Use known character sequence and controlled elapsed intervals; compare transitions, calculated speed/accuracy and terminal replay effects; B forbidden and target/other DB rows compared.
Explicit page DTO values and training ID; exact owner-scoped projections, B denied.
Compare status, character scoring, time accumulation and duplicate-finish behavior with DB snapshots.

Separate harness sends identical UTF-8 file bytes under multipart field file, preserves preview array values, then sends the JSON add DTO. Compare preview semantics and saved rows; ordinary user cannot perform admin add.
Compare content, IDs and null result for missing type.
C updates seeded type; D/E denied; requested type changes only. Do not infer owner policy from anonymous rejection.
Compare tree shape, page arrays, legacy listPge spelling and ownership filtering.
C may move/insert within seeded tree, D/E denied; compare parent relationships, order and unrelated branches in DB.
A transitions only own ready/running fixtures; compare time/score/count values and terminal replay, B denial and unchanged foreign records.
Compare non-zero aggregates, report fields, numeric score and owner-only detail.
Compare elapsed intervals, report logs and final scoring; repeated finish and foreign train request cannot alter settled rows.
Same type results are scoped to authenticated owner; JSON arrays/types preserved.
A writes/clears only A rows even with forged user field; compare calculation, deleted keys and B unchanged rows.
Compare non-zero totals, numeric scores and exact owner list.
Compare persisted text/value arrays, server scores and own deletion; B cannot read/delete A record and B rows remain unchanged.
Non-zero score/speed/accuracy and owner-only detail match exactly.
Compare pause-excluded timing and server scoring; reject foreign/terminal submissions and verify no second settlement.
Capture per-backend session ID, submit once and compare session consumption, saved train and replay rejection; cannot compare generated IDs without mapping.
Compare owner list, detail and ordered floor text, not just response envelope.
Compare ordered page/log writes, pause/finish timing, score and terminal replay; verify floor and train rows and unchanged foreign training.
Compare seeded pageNumber bounds, owner filtering and null/error on absent page.
Match per-page score/time arrays, final state, reset attempt and stale/replayed page rejection with page/train DB snapshots.
Compare trainType query plus JSON paging, page boundaries and owner restriction.
Compare partial-page settlement and receipt arrays, paused time exclusion, attempt transitions and duplicate/stale rejection; DB writes checked independently.
Compare page/setting/masthead shapes and denied foreign ownership.
Preserve upload JSON arrays instead of string coercion; compare score/time/state/attempt and terminal replay effects.
Masthead owner scope and setting admin scope are separate cases; compare target and unrelated DB rows.
Compare rule projections, own details and forbidden foreign details.
Verify server answer scoring and submission replay; only C may change rules. Compare rule/train/answer snapshots and generated-ID correlation.
Each family must compare non-empty list/detail/page/value/statistics for participant and controller; outsider denied.

Run each family: controller starts, participant submits ordered JSON arrays, final partial page settles, duplicate/stale attempt rejected, reset/recovery cannot double-settle. Compare train/user/page/result rows after each barrier.
Separate stateful WS harness: connect two users, compare online REST projections, replace one session, stale old close must retain the new session; disconnect is local until settlement rules apply.
Compare all four room types, member visibility and creator/outsider permissions; fixed room content and channel order.
Compare channel/finish/upload JSON transitions, roomId query binding for sendFinish and member authorization; DB records plus broadcast recipients/order must agree.

Java inventory declares admin route, but current Rust main.rs has no matching registered route. Requires application route coverage before any shared fixture can be marked runnable; admin versus ordinary/no-role behavior remains pending.
Compare A aggregates, explicit year query, no B leakage and array ordering. Database/clock setup required; anonymous code203 does not prove report parity.
Exact returned fields/types and matching selected rule; no string-to-number coercion.
JSON add is an array of rule DTOs, not a multipart request or object wrapper. C succeeds, D/E denied; compare requested type rows and unrelated type unchanged.

assertions_required: Upgrade both endpoints; exchange __nip_heartbeat_ping__ and require __nip_heartbeat_pong__; send arbitrary text and require pong. Record opcode, payload, close status and ordering.

setup: A/B authenticated query-only credentials; path sid deliberately differs from authenticated identity.
assertions_required: Missing/invalid query credentials produce error frame and close; header credentials cannot replace query authentication.
Drive one valid and one malformed capture; compare response model, owner restriction and DB effect.
Connect replacement A session, then close old A; only the newest session can mutate A state.

setup: Two members/controller/outsider and fixed room state; path sid is route-only.
assertions_required: Compare RequestModel dispatch, unknown/malformed code=-1 frames, recipient sets and room transitions.
Duplicate A session closes/notifies old generation; delayed old close must not evict new generation.

setup: Fixed creator/member/outsider, room type, channel and room ID; mismatched path user ID cannot change identity.
assertions_required: Compare handshake membership, heartbeat, valid channel/topic broadcasts and malformed/unauthorized errors.
Correlate REST projection and DB transition; replacement session/stale close preserves new membership.

setup: Controller role=1, participant role=0, outsider; fixed numeric train ID, attempts and pages.
assertions_required: Compare ready/begin/pat/finish/end dispatch, wrong-role and malformed frames, ordered broadcasts and REST/DB settlement.
Identity comes from query token, not uid; stale old close cannot remove replacement.

setup: Same role matrix with an opaque string train ID, exact message/body arrays and fixed time.
assertions_required: Compare ready/begin/pat/finish/end, malformed and wrong-role errors and capture-array typing.
Compare final partial-page settlement and replacement/stale-close behavior across REST/WS/DB.

setup: Controller/participant/outsider with numeric train ID and role path that must match server membership.
assertions_required: Compare role mismatch handshake, ready/begin/pat/finish/end, malformed frames and final-page scoring.
Replace same user/role session; delayed old close and failed-recipient cleanup must not remove new session.

scope_boundary: No runtime checks, backend requests or commits were performed for this revision. Domain lifecycle, owner/admin, DB writes, multipart and WS assertions are specified requirements only. Readiness to execute a case is not evidence it passed.
